newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra provides A$81.5 mln drought relief.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra provides A$81.5 mln drought relief.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Monday the government would provide farmers with A$81.5 million for drought recovery.

"I'm announcing an A$81.5 million drought recovery package which centres on an extension of the drought recovery period following the revokation of drought exceptional circumstances from six months to 12 months," Anderson told reporters.

Anderson said the decision was largely based on the rural sector's problems of re-establishing cashflow given the conditions in the wool and beef industries, and partly the ongoing difficulties of long-term drought in eastern Australia.
Farmers in regions where Drought Exceptional Circumstances (DEC) was revoked in June could now apply for day-to-day drought relief payment for a further six months to June 1997, Anderson said.
Included in the package was A$10 million for herd and flock rebuilding and pasture re-establishment, and A$1.5 million for enhanced re-establishment grants.
"Farmers will be able to apply during the 12 month drought recovery period and required to exit farming within 12 months of the cessation of the recovery period," he said.
Re-establishment payments would allow for grants of up to A$45,000 for exiting farmers and additional support of A$30,000 for eligible farmers in revoked or current DEC areas.
Funding for education, family, health and rural financial counsellors would also be extended in these areas.
"In areas where the drought has broken, the government recognises that it will take time to recover, and many farmers will need ongoing support during this period," he said.
But he said in many areas the drought had not yet broken.
"The range of assistance measures provided by the Commonwealth to farmers in these areas will continue."
